To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth of CNC/Ge-imolite films is governed by the surface charge density of imogolite nanotubes and that the aspect ratio of imolite nanotube has an impact on the film growth.
the growth mode of CNC/Ge-imolite films differs from that of CNC/PE and Ge-imogilite/PE films.
the growth of CNC/Ge-imolite (NP/ NP) films is different from the growth of CNC or Ge- imogolites combined to polyelectrolys (NP/PE) films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of multilayered thin film by layer-by-layer deposition method using two oppositely charges nanoparticles (NPs).
the preparation of CNC/Ge-imolite multilayered thin film and the impact of the different parameters on the film growth.
the elaboration of multilayered thin film combining two oppositively charged NPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of CNC/Ge-imolite multilayered thin film was governed by a combination of the surface charge and the surface packing.
the growth mode of multilayered NP/NP films is governed by the balance between electrostatic attraction and steric hindrance.
the film growth pattern is a function of the nature of the NPs, their aspect ratio, and the ionic strength of the solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NP/NP films are formed by a different mechanism than NP/PE films.
NP/NP films growth patterns are more complex than NP/PE films.
the NP/NP multilayers are a good candidate to be used as a model system for the development of new functional nanomaterials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to obtain multilayered thin film by the layer-by layer method combining oppositely charged NPs, but it requires a careful choice of NPs, and a precise control of the experimental conditions.
NP/NP thin films can be successfully prepared and their architecture can be controlled by tuning the aspect ratio of imogoilites and the drying step.
NP/NP films are more stable than NP/PE films, which can be used for the fabrication of more robust nanomaterials.
